text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finland not making full use of its skilled immigrant labour as many immigrants remain unemployed.
- One in every seven young Finns is a racist, while a third see racism as a big problem in Finland, survey shows.
- International copyright rules may endanger the situation of libraries in the information society, Finnish library society says. @
- Finnish forest industry says mill stoppages this year will cost it over seven billion markka in lost export revenues.
- President Martti Ahtisaari on official visit to India spoke of his concern over Finland's unemployment problem and said he would address the issue more broadly this year.
- Environmental activists' campaign to curb Christmas consumerism lacks bite as retail sales expected to soar this year. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Former KOP bank chiefs denied in court accusations that they made unfounded promises to the public during the bank's 1994 share issue.
- Tax-free bank deposits have increased markedly and somewhat unexpectedly this year, says Merita executive Eino Halonen.
- Firms exporting food-processing technology see good prospects in Russia where investment in the sector growing.
- International advertisers often regard the Nordic countries as a homogenous entity despite clear differences. @
AAMULEHTI
- Forest industry to shift from regional wood purchase agreements to company-by-company contracts next year.
DEMARI

- Finnish transport workers' union AKT ended action that had halted unloading of Russian trucks in protest against treatment of Finnish truckers in Russia. Finnish transport ministry assured truckers that it is taking the problem seriously. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Police have left hundreds of positions vacant because of tight budget. Police union spokesman says 2.4 billion markka budgeted for 1997 falls 200-300 million short of need.
- Finns and Swedes design new saw to prune by helicopter tree tops interfering with power lines.
